title: QBR metrics decision worksheet and operators guide
content:
Purpose:

This is an operator-focused worksheet + playbook for Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) that translates low-level infra/serving metrics into customer-facing renewal signals and recommended actions. Intended use: CS reps preparing QBRs, solutions engineers doing pre-renewal risk triage, and SRE/observability on-call when customers see degradations.

Quick definitions (operator-friendly):
- Latency (generation): typical latency percentiles for token-generating endpoints. We report p50, p95, p99 for end-to-end request completion (includes routing + queue + inference).
  - p50: median observed over the reporting window (default: 7 days).
  - p95: upper-bound for common tail behaviors (use for customer SLAs).
  - p99: extreme tail — indicates systemic queuing or hot-shard issues.
- Uptime: percent of time the customer’s configured route returned successful 2xx responses (or configured fallback) in the window. Count excludes planned maintenance windows where we provided notice.
- Cost / token: effective per-token cost as billed/attributed to the customer in the window (includes model variant multipliers, batching discounts, and any dedicated capacity surcharges). Expressed in $ per 1k tokens.
- Cache hit rate: fraction of token-seconds or requests satisfied from prefix/KV cache (depending on instrumentation). We include both request-level hit-rate and token-level hit-rate where available.

Measurement details and formulas (how we compute the numbers you will read in dashboards):
- Windowing: default 7d rolling for QBR snapshots; 30d for trend analysis.
- Latency aggregates: compute percentiles on request completion times after outlier removal (drop top/bottom 0.1% to remove test traffic and instrumentation glitches).
- Cost/token calculation: (total_billed_usd / total_generated_or_consumed_tokens) * 1000 -> $/1k tokens. If a customer has a dedicated capacity surcharge, annotate separately.
- Cache hit formatting: present as two metrics: request_hit_rate = cache_hits / cacheable_requests and token_hit_rate = cached_tokens / total_tokens_generated.

KPI snapshot template (paste into QBR slide or use as checklist):
- Customer: <NAME>
- Reporting window: <7d / 30d>
- Latency p50: <ms>
- Latency p95: <ms>
- Latency p99: <ms>
- Uptime: <99.xx%> (exclude planned maintenance)
- Cost per 1k tokens: <$0.XX>
- Request cache hit rate: <%>
- Token cache hit rate: <%>
- Query volume: <requests/day> / <tokens/day>
- Error rate (4xx/5xx): <%>

Sample KPI table (text representation you can paste into Google Slides):
| Segment | p50 ms | p95 ms | p99 ms | uptime % | cost/1k tokens | req cache % | token cache % | notes |
| Small (pilot) | 120 | 340 | 920 | 99.8 | $0.45 | 12 | 18 | batched, low concurrency |
| Mid | 85 | 210 | 640 | 99.95 | $0.32 | 21 | 34 | mixed workloads, caching tuned |
| Enterprise | 60 | 150 | 420 | 99.99 | $0.22 | 48 | 62 | dedicated pools, KV caching |

Decision rules (human-readable heuristics used in renewal scoring):
- Green (low risk): uptime >= 99.95 AND p95 <= historical SLA target AND cost/1k tokens within expected band (<= baseline +10%) AND token cache >= customer_benchmark -> recommend standard renewal.
- Yellow (medium risk): any single metric degraded (e.g., p95 up 30% vs baseline OR cost/1k tokens increased >20% without corresponding value gains) -> schedule technical healthcheck, propose cost-optimization session (Optimize team).
- Red (high risk): multiple metrics degraded OR uptime < 99.9 OR p99 > 2x baseline AND cache token hit rate < 10% despite disabled conservative caching -> immediate escalation: SE + SRE + CSM sync, consider temporary credits or model routing changes.

Operator playbook (triage checklist — use during pre-QBR run or post-incident):
1) Confirm scope: which routes/models are customer-critical? Pull route-level polyline from Console.
2) Recompute KPIs for last 7 days and 30 days (to see whether spike is transient). Use: Confluence runbook -> JMX/metrics query example (linked below).
3) If latency tail is high: check queue lengths, autoscaler events, GPU utilization, and kernel failures. Escalate to serving-runtime team if autoscaler indicates backpressure for >30m.
4) If cost/token jumped: inspect model variant usage, sampling rate changes, or enablement of higher-cost features (streaming vs non-streaming, function-calls). Run cost breakdown in Console (token types).
5) If cache hit rate is low: validate cache keying (are customers calling with unique prefixes?), check cache size and eviction metrics, and verify KV latency. Suggest prefix-preserving template changes for customers.
6) For uptime issues: cross-check global routing fallbacks, region-specific incidents, and whether a dedicated pool fallback was in use.

Renewal conversation prompts (CS framing):
- Value story: "Over the last quarter you reduced average latency by X% and token cost by Y% — this translates to $Z monthly savings at your current volume."
- Risk story: "We flagged a sustained p95 increase driven by a high-variability route. If we don't stabilize it, it increases error surface and could impact your user-facing SLAs."
- Action ask: "We recommend a 60-minute PS session to tune caching and batching; options include a 3-week dedicated optimization engagement or a self-serve checklist we can walk through."

Example snapshots (realistic numbers to copy):
- Pilot customer (high churn risk): p95 up 45% vs baseline, uptime 99.70, cost/1k tokens up 38%, token cache 6% -> Action: immediate SE deep-dive + 10% renewal discount contingent on remediation plan.
- Strategic customer (low churn risk): p95 stable, uptime 99.995, cost/1k tokens flat, token cache 58% -> Action: present value story, propose expansion to Dedicated for further unit-cost improvements.

Notes to self / known gaps (what this doc does NOT capture yet):
- We don't standardize a single "token" definition across some integrated customers (upstream may rewrite tokens in proxy) — annotate per-customer if unusual.
- We need a backend query that emits token-level cache hit rate per-route (work item: JIRA CS-3059).
- Attribution of dedicated surcharge into cost/token isn't surfaced in public console UI; currently only in billing exports.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Create a one-click QBR snapshot in Console that exports the table above (owner: Priya, due: 2025-02-01).
- [ ] Add token-level cache metric to telemetry (owner: SRE, linked JIRA CS-3059).
- [ ] Draft an email template for "pre-QBR health summary" using these fields (owner: Diego).

Unresolved questions:
- Should we use 7d or 14d as primary QBR window? 7d is more responsive, 30d better for trend smoothing. Recommend 7d for actionability, 30d for trend slide.
- Which cost bands do we show in the public QBR deck for Pilots vs Enterprise? (Need product/finance input).

References and queries to copy into runbooks:
- Console query example (token-level): confluence://metrics/token-query-template
- SRE runbook for autoscaler backpressure: confluence://runbooks/autoscaler-backpressure
- Jira tickets: JIRA-CS-2745 (QBR objectives), JIRA-CS-3059 (telemetry gap)

Notes: this file is a working operator artifact; paste sections into Google Slides or the QBR template as needed. Keep a short change log at the top of the next revision.
